newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates up amid select buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates up amid select buying.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose slightly on Saturday in selective buying of good quality stocks by mill owners, and are likely to gain further on demand from exporters, dealers said.
Mill owners were short of funds and went only for quality stocks pushing up the Karachi Cotton Association's (KCA) spot rates, dealer Kishan Chand said.

"The prices can rise further if exporters start buying," he said. "But right now there is no major demand as the mill owners expect incentives from the new government while exporters too are in a wait-and-see mood."
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted between 2,000 ($49.72) and 2,050 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), the K-68 between 2,250 to 2,300 and the MNH-93 at 2,300 rupees.
